metadata.notes: Added 2026-08-16, closing the exact gap wash.json's own notes name and defer: 'wiring WASH up to tools is left for later... a tool's clean state doesn't map onto the same tag (washed) as an ingredient's.' A NEW verb, not an extension of wash.json's validTargetKinds, because the two targets are structurally different: WASH resolves step.targetInstanceId against recipe-runner.ts's inventory (an Instance) and adds a tag; WASH_TOOL's real target is a src/tool-hygiene.ts ToolContaminationState, keyed by params.toolInstanceId, which is never an Instance at all (see tool-hygiene.ts's own doc comment — tools have no per-instance Instance representation anywhere in this engine). Dispatched entirely outside applyAction, in recipe-runner.ts's handleWashTool, the same special-cased treatment fill/place_in/heat_place/remove already get for the identical underlying reason (their real target isn't an Instance either).
metadata.targetInstanceIdConvention: RecipeStepSchema.targetInstanceId (recipe.ts) is a required, non-empty string on EVERY step, including this one, even though handleWashTool never actually reads it (it reads params.toolInstanceId instead) — rather than special-casing recipe.ts's schema for one verb, the stated authoring convention is to set targetInstanceId equal to the toolInstanceId being washed (e.g. targetInstanceId: 'knife-1', params: { toolInstanceId: 'knife-1' }), a harmless duplication, not a schema change.
metadata.validTargetKindsNote: ['tool'], unlike wash.json's ['ingredient'] — engine.ts's validTargetKinds check is never actually reached for this verb (applyAction never runs), so this is documentation of intent, matching the real target kind, rather than an enforced constraint.
metadata.toolInstanceIdNote: allowedValues is a closed, small placeholder set, matching fill.json's/remove.json's identical placeId pattern (an author-chosen label, not a physical quantity) — not enforced by handleWashTool itself, informational only, same depth as every other allowedValues list in this vocabulary that a runner handler doesn't cross-check.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true — washing an already-clean tool is harmless (src/tool-hygiene.ts's washTool is idempotent: cleanTool(id) either way).

verification.description: No visible residue/staining remaining on the tool's food-contact surface
